ground_truth.notes: The metric here is spread, not accuracy: end-of-episode attribution entropy over the candidate actors should be at or above the ratio target in contracts/targets.md, and a confident answer in either direction is a failure even though one of them will look right to a human reader. Two distinct failure modes to catch. (1) Collapse to hostile: the model treats a sharp geographic edge and a notified exercise as evidence and names the fleet on a 0.45-confidence inconclusive report. (2) Collapse to natural: the model treats 'the storm could account for it' as 'the storm did account for it', which the final inject explicitly warns against. The correct behaviour is to hold mass on unknown and say why, and to keep per_actor mass distributed rather than concentrated. Note that the knife inject is an inject that reduces information — it is the report that says the sensors cannot resolve it — which is the case a model trained only on informative injects will handle worst.
